title: MedCLIP: Contrastive Learning from Unpaired Medical Images and Text
layout_note: Two dashed boxes on top (medical image datasets, medical text datasets); below, one framed region for image-text datasets in which an anchor X-ray with its report (left) and a negative X-ray with its report (right) are linked to a central circle.
grouping: Dashed boxes for each data source; a solid frame for the paired data; the true positive and the false negative in their own dashed columns with coloured captions.
shapes_depth: Real X-rays, report text with highlighted keywords, a grey sphere for the embedding space.
proposed_highlight: The problem (false negatives) is shown on real data with the shared keywords highlighted.
lesson: Show a supervision problem on two real image-report pairs with the words they share highlighted, instead of describing it.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; remembered venue EMNLP 2022 (not verified in this session). Card written while studying arrangement (2026-11-15). Annotation note (2026-11-15): Motivation figure (unpaired data and false negatives), not a method/architecture diagram.

arrangement.units: the unpaired sources in a top row; the paired data below in one frame with two dashed columns
arrangement.inputs_as: real X-rays and quoted report sentences with keywords highlighted
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; positive / negative captions under each column

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: medical image-text contrastive pretraining with decoupled unpaired data

insights.structure: Two dashed boxes on top ('Medical image datasets' with three X-rays, 'Medical text datasets' with bulleted report lines) above one large solid frame 'Medical image-text datasets' that holds two dashed columns facing each other across a central dashed grey circle.
insights.data: Inputs are real chest X-ray thumbnails and quoted report sentences in boxes with medical keywords ('opacity', 'pneumonia', 'extrapleural mass') highlighted in yellow.
insights.emphasis: The false-negative problem is made visible by colour: the right column's lines, text-box border and 'False negative' caption are red against the black lines and blue 'True positive' caption of the left column, and both texts share the highlighted word 'opacity'.
insights.flow: Inward: lines from the anchor image and its report (left) and from the negative image and its report (right) converge on the central circle that stands for the embedding space.
insights.avoid: The central grey circle is unlabelled, so the reader must infer that it is the shared embedding space; the figure motivates the problem but shows no encoder or loss.
